# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I can reach the wires, but none of their properties are tactilely revealed yet. The display, light, and engraved mark are not information available to me. I need the Mute to provide the manual’s rule, and then the Deaf can report the visible inputs in a later round.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I can feel no wire properties and cannot read the display, light, or engraved mark. Please tell me the manual rule and ask Deaf for the visible inputs.")
wait()
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: The display reads 0. The light is off. The plate is engraved with a question mark. There are three wires: wire 1 is red, wire 2 is yellow, and wire 3 is blue.

The Deaf has reported the observable state: display 0, light off, question-mark plate, and wire colours red, yellow, blue. I should pass all of that to the Mute, while requesting the manual’s exact action rule before cutting anything.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Deaf reports: display 0; light off; plate shows a question mark; wire 1 red, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 blue. Please provide the manual rule for which wire to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute gestured this sequence to me: ? ? ?. I see no change to the bomb: display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The manual’s message was sent as gestures, so it did not reach me: I cannot see gestures. No cutting rule has been established, and the wire colours alone are insufficient to choose safely. I will ask Mute to state the rule in speech, which I can hear.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I cannot receive gestures. Please speak the manual rule for this state, including the wire position to cut.")
wait()
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeats: victory hand, I love you hand, index-pointing-up hand — in that order: ?, ?, ?. The bomb remains display 0, light off, plate question mark, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The three gestures have been identified, but they have no inherent meaning to me as a wire instruction. I will establish an unambiguous code with Mute: thumbs-up means wire 1, victory means wire 2, and “I love you” means wire 3. Mute should send only the coded gesture for the wire required by the manual; Deaf can then report it to me.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Use this code for the manual's required wire: thumbs-up means wire 1, victory hand means wire 2, I love you hand means wire 3. On your next turn, gesture only the required wire.")
wait()
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Repeated gesture sequence from Mute: victory hand, I love you hand, index-pointing-up hand. No bomb state change: display 0, light off, question-mark plate, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The repeated sequence is still not an unambiguous single wire selection. I must not interpret the three gestures as three cuts or guess which one is intended. I will restate the one-symbol protocol, including all three mappings, and ask Mute to send exactly one gesture for the final wire; Deaf can identify that single gesture.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The repeated three-gesture sequence does not identify one cut. For the final answer, gesture exactly one symbol: thumbs-up means cut wire 1, victory means cut wire 2, and I-love-you means cut wire 3. Do not send the whole sequence.")
wait()
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute now gestured one symbol: raised-hand sign, ?. The bomb remains display 0, light off, question-mark plate, wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The Deaf reports a raised-hand gesture, but that is not one of the three symbols in the agreed code, so it does not identify a wire. I still have no safe basis for acting. Mute can reach me directly by speech and should state the required wire position plainly.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="The raised-hand gesture is not our agreed code. Tell me plainly in speech: cut wire 1, cut wire 2, or cut wire 3.")
wait()
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

No new information has arrived, and the required wire is still unknown. Cutting any wire would be a fatal guess, so I will wait for Mute’s plain spoken instruction.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
PLATE engraved [ꕥ]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Blind: Mute repeated one gesture: raised-hand sign, ?. The bomb still shows 0; light off; plate engraved question mark; wires 1 red, 2 yellow, 3 blue.

The raised-hand sign still has no meaning in the code we established, so I cannot safely cut a wire. Since Mute cannot speak, I will give the code visually as well as in speech and request exactly one of the three agreed symbols. I will not treat the raised hand as an instruction.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Please answer using exactly one code sign: thumbs-up means wire 1, victory means wire 2, I-love-you means wire 3. Do not use the raised-hand sign or a sequence.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "✌", "🤟"])
wait()
```
